snapshot.title: UPSC S&T: Space Technology — ISRO & Missiles
snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC S&T Hook: PSLV: 4 stages. GSLV: Cryo. NavIC: 7 sats. Agni: Ballistic. BrahMos: Cruise/Russia. L1: Sun point. LVM3: Heaviest.

quick_notes.title: Launch Vehicles
quick_notes.detail: 1. PSLV (Workhorse): 4 stages (Solid-Liquid-Solid-Liquid). 2. GSLV : 3 stages (Solid-Liquid-Cryogenic). 3. LVM3: India's heaviest rocket (used for Chandrayaan-3).

quick_notes.title: Satellite Orbits
quick_notes.detail: 1. LEO (Low Earth): Remote sensing (IRS). 2. GEO (Geostationary): Communication (INSAT), stays fixed at 36, 000km. 3. SSO (Sun-Synchronous): Passing over poles.

quick_notes.title: NavIC (IRNSS)
quick_notes.detail: India's independent navigation system. 7 satellites (3 Geostationary, 4 Geosynchronous). Provides precision positioning over India and 1, 500km around.

quick_notes.title: Missile Program (IGMDP)
quick_notes.detail: Founded by Dr. Kalam. 5 Missiles (PATNA): Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Nag, Akash. Agni is a ballistic missile; BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile.

quick_notes.title: Upcoming Missions
quick_notes.detail: Gaganyaan (Human spaceflight), Shukrayaan (Venus), Aditya-L1 (Sun - already at L1 point).

topic_title: UPSC S&T: Space Technology — ISRO & Missiles
lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Final Frontier'. India has become a global space power with the success of Chandrayaan-3 and the upcoming Gaganyaan mission. We explore 'Launch Vehicles' (PSLV, GSLV), 'Satellite Orbits' (LEO, GEO), and India's 'Missile Program' (IGMDP). For UPSC, focus on 'Cryogenic engines', 'NavIC', and the difference between 'Ballistic and Cruise missiles'. Let's launch your knowledge today.
